description: Analysys Mason, a telecoms, media and technology consultancy, sells a Communications Infrastructure Data research programme that its page describes as detailed data, insights and forecasts on the physical and spectrum elements of global communications. Coverage: separate modules track cell sites, data centres, spectrum and space; the page describes tracking and forecasts of investment, ownership, traffic and usage of infrastructure. Recent research trackers listed on the page include a cells and sites database (September 2026) and data centre databases for North America and for the Middle East and Africa (August 2026). Format and access: subscription research; subscribers also get a client enquiry service. A separate DataHub interface gives subscribers historical and forecast data from the Telecoms and Media Data, IT Data and Space programmes, with on-screen charts, filtering and export to Excel; the DataHub page states around 2,150 telecoms metrics, about 120,000 IT spending metrics and nearly 4,000 space metrics from 18 forecast reports. Cost: paid; prices were not read. Licence: proprietary; subscription terms were not read. Caveats: the page does not say whether the communications infrastructure trackers themselves are in DataHub, nor give the fields, country coverage or asset-level detail of the cell site and data centre databases. Simulation uses: counts and ownership of cell sites and data centres by market, and capacity forecasts, as context for telecom network exposure and capacity studies.
